correctness.rationale: For every admissible observed density, total variation on the extended space equals the maximum of its positive and negative observed-density discrepancy masses. Monotonicity of the Gaussian likelihood ratio identifies the two unavoidable tails, and the pointwise clipped density attains both simultaneously. The Mills expansion yields \(A_b(r)\sim C_bS^{-3/2}e^{-S}\) with \(C_b=\sqrt b\,\log(1/b)/(4\sqrt\pi)\); the lower clip is super-polynomially smaller at the critical scale. Tensorization plus the same testing reduction as Proposition 22 gives the interval lower bound. No experiment is used as proof.

value.rationale: The exact total-variation modulus is the natural testing invariant controlling the adaptive confidence lower bound. It replaces coarse casewise constants by a single exact formula, exposes a genuine \(-3/2\) log-log threshold, and strengthens the fixed-MCAR leading lower coefficient to \(\log(1/(1-\epsilon))/\sqrt2\). Because the source problem converges only at logarithmic speed, the coefficient and second-order window materially affect the information-theoretic boundary rather than constituting a routine algebraic restatement.
